scope: First adapter identity and ownership increment within the broader catalog redesign
Proposed Kontakt boundaries, manifest precedence, ambiguity, and selected scope
SINE vendor identities and complete scoped installed microphone membership
Context tags versus instrument-specific searchable metadata

reviewed_documents: .work/active/library-catalog-redesign.md: relevant identity, adapter, and ordered-delivery contracts
verdict: PASS: no blocking issues for this scoped identity foundation increment.
rationale: The increment supplies adapter relationships before persistence and outline adoption, consistent with the broader plan's requirement for SQLite before replacing the tree.
Kontakt layout inference remains proposed rather than vendor-confirmed; explicit ambiguity, nested-product, overlapping-root, and scope-boundary tests protect neighboring libraries.
SINE identities are namespaced vendor IDs rather than paths or display names, while each installed scoped microphone metadata/archive pair remains represented.
Per-instrument effective tags cannot inherit sibling search summaries, and optional additive fields preserve decoding of prior reports.
The four-host deliverable records acceptance fixtures and unknown status, without pretending that an evidence matrix implements DAW compatibility.
Read-only local validation and deterministic regression fixtures are proportionate to the adapter change; no deletion, new persisted state, fabricated dates, or storage totals are included.
limitations: Specification critique only; implementation and runtime output remain subject to independent review and the documented gates.
This increment does not deliver durable identity across sessions, the replacement hierarchy UI, storage accounting, or validated usage adapters.
No product code changed; no holdout or private user content accessed.
